title: Host-side inference credential boundary: provider keys stay on host
reasoning: Remote Hermes workers currently lack a configured inference provider. scripts/harness/install-hermes.sh:90-94 requires a provider-key variable in node ~/.hermes/.env, and the original CF-002 acceptance criterion required that node-local key. This conflicts with the owner policy that provider API keys remain on the control host. Implement an authenticated host-side inference gateway/proxy; the node receives only a dedicated revocable service identity scoped to node/project/repository and allowed models. Finalize the transport boundary with the Crier/gateway design, and do not claim live end-to-end proof until an authorized disposable node exists.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Provider API keys remain only on the control host; none appear in node ~/.hermes/.env, node manifests, Crier identity bundles, argv, logs, artifacts, or the repository. A synthetic sentinel proves installers and transport never forward an upstream provider key.
2. Remote Hermes requests use an authenticated host-side inference gateway/proxy. A node receives only a dedicated, revocable service identity (not a provider key), scoped to one node/project/repository and an explicit model allowlist; upstream provider credentials are resolved only on the host.
3. The host-side gateway rejects missing, malformed, expired, revoked, wrong-node/project, and disallowed-model requests before provider-key resolution. Tests prove fail-closed behavior and no secret values in errors or logs.
4. Requested versus served model/provider is recorded in immutable usage evidence; tests prove fallback remains within the authorized model allowlist.
5. Live end-to-end testing requires an owner-authorized disposable remote node and private authenticated host-side endpoint. This task does not authorize key transfer or provisioning; document blockers and the host-only boundary in specs/HARNESS.md and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md.

title: Node sizing and disk policy: refuse admission with the number
reasoning: Measured: 4.3 GB free inside an agent on a host at 97%, while one repo node costs ~1.5 GB and sibling agents swing free space by 5 GB. Without a policy nodes fill the host and fail mid-job, which is the orphaned-work failure this fleet has already had.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A documented floor per node role, justified by measured footprint. 2. The ladder refuses admission below the floor, naming the number, before any install begins. 3. A reclaim step (build cache, job dirs, stale clones) runs before refusal. 4. A boundary test proves the refusal fires. 5. bunker status residue (orphan homes/keys/users) is reaped and reported.

title: Node lifecycle: supervisor, renew, destroy/rebuild
reasoning: A node's gateway is started with nohup and dies on agent stop/renew; agent TTL is 4h unless renewed. A node that silently disappears is indistinguishable from a node that failed, and cancellation is only possible by killing the process group from a second exec (client kill and --timeout do NOT stop remote work).
acceptance_criteria: 1. The harness runs under a supervisor that restarts it and records restarts. 2. Agent TTL is renewed automatically while the node is active. 3. Cancelling a dispatch kills the process GROUP and the evidence shows it (job pid/pgid written by the job, killed, completion artifact absent after the deadline). 4. destroy then create reproduces the node from recorded commands with no manual step. 5. A node that dies mid-job causes redelivery, and idempotency prevents duplicated work.

title: Align Code Factory PM, QA, dogfood, and support lanes with fleet invariants
reasoning: The live scheduler invariant audit previously flagged seven Code Factory satellite workdirs without a resolvable target board and 12 cooldown_s=900 values below the six-hour floor/family cadences. User explicitly requests the PM, QA, dogfood and other standard lanes to participate; enabled-but-unrunnable is not coverage.
acceptance_criteria: 1. For each enabled code-factory satellite, verify its canonical namespace, parent, prompt, target project, and workdir against live peer conventions and ops/check-fleet-invariants.py. 2. Ensure PM, QA, dogfood, docs-qa, readme-qa, releng-qa, sync, and other registered satellites resolve an owned, valid board root; do not create duplicate shared boards. 3. Replace sub-floor cooldown values only through the scheduler family policy and explicit canonical pins; preserve lane intent and read back both DB/API and fleet config. 4. Sync lane has a README/orientation and a findable consumption contract. 5. Run the invariant checker and board validation; any unresolved check is recorded as a blocker, not masked by disabling a lane. 6. Do not force a live dispatch until each lane has dispatchable work and its board writer boundary is verified.

title: Specify and implement the secure node-side Crier pull/reply adapter
reasoning: Independent QA review found that DESIGN/ENVELOPE specify the intended Crier path, but the tracked repo has no complete Crier pull/reply worker or secure identity staging. CF-001 and CF-004 cannot pass live without this seam.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Define the node-side Crier identity and pull/reply contract using the existing envelope spec; keep any Crier server change on a separate Crier-owned row/repo. 2. Stage exactly one mode-600 identity bundle through an approved transfer path; never expose secret values in argv, logs, boards, or artifacts; delete the bundle after use and fail closed on absence, bad permissions, or revocation. 3. Validate envelope digest, reserved-key rules, correlation/idempotency, and dispatch identity before invoking the configured harness; acknowledge only after a verified result is delivered. 4. Add contract tests for malformed/reserved envelopes, duplicate delivery, gateway failure, failed result delivery, and ack-after-result semantics. 5. Live Crier/inference testing remains blocked until explicitly owner-authorized credentials and a disposable remote node exist; mocks do not count as live proof.

title: Re-run targeted CF-005 quorum after credential and node-script fixes
reasoning: The 2026-10-30 targeted quorum found a false-positive selftest red arm, node-credential policy conflict, missing repo precondition, artifact path overreach, and manifest write/reuse failures. This is the required re-evaluation after the existing CF-002 and CF-005 rows land; the full design quorum remains CF-021.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Run only after CF-002 and CF-005 are complete and their merged commits are available.
2. Reproduce the named project-node check failure with bootstrap tools present; prove a targeted mutation causes selftest failure, and prove FAILED: unbound variable cannot satisfy the red arm.
3. Verify node-create rejects absent repo/harness before spawn and captures the exact valid triple; verify-node rejects credential/config paths before remote execution; verify manifest write failure and identity mismatch fail closed.
4. Confirm specs and threat model match measured source and the host-only provider-key policy; no provider key is present on a node.
5. Run clean-tree selftest, board validation, and the relevant full guard. Convene at least three independently routed model families, verify served identity/provider, and publish an auditable re-review artifact with dispositions.
6. Do not claim live remote execution unless an owner-authorized disposable node and authenticated host-side inference path actually run; otherwise record that proof as blocked.
